title: How the Nobel Peace Prize Works
summary: Josh and Chuck open with banter about cocktails (the Chuck B drink), then discuss the Nobel Peace Prize: its origin in Alfred Nobel's will, Nobel's background as dynamite inventor and arms-family heir, the apocryphal "merchant of death" obituary story, the will's legal fight and transport of the money to the Swedish embassy, the prize's funding and cash value, the Norwegian Nobel Committee and its selection process, nominations and the 50-year secrecy rule, eras and controversies (Kissinger and Le Duc Tho, Obama, Aung San Suu Kyi, Abiy Ahmed, Gandhi snub), the medal design, and the Right Livelihood Award alternative. The episode closes with a listener mail about whether brownies are cookies.

segments.title: Opening banter and cocktail talk
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck joke about Chuck's homemade 'Chuck B' cocktail, with egg white, honey syrup and ginger liqueur, then set up the episode's subject: the Nobel Peace Prize.

segments.title: Nominations are not an honor; who is Nobel
segments.summary: The hosts note that anyone can be nominated and that a nomination alone carries little honor. They mention that Mussolini, Stalin and Hitler were nominated, and tease a fifty-year mystery about who nominated Bono. They then introduce Alfred Nobel as the inventor of dynamite.

segments.title: Alfred Nobel's family, early life and the nitroglycerin accident
segments.summary: The hosts describe Alfred's father Manuel, who moved the family to Russia to make weapons, and Alfred's education and eccentric personality. They cover the 1864 nitroglycerin explosion that killed his brother and others, his move of the lab onto a barge, and his development of dynamite.

segments.title: The merchant of death obituary myth
segments.summary: The hosts relate the story, which may be apocryphal, that a French newspaper printed Alfred's obituary by mistake after his brother Ludwig died, calling him the 'merchant of death'. They say historians have not found the original article and discuss how this may have prompted his change of heart.

segments.title: Nobel's will, legal fight and the money transport
segments.summary: Nobel died in December 1896 with a fortune of around three hundred million dollars in today's terms. His will set up prizes, but heirs contested it, and the executor drove the cash through Paris to the Swedish embassy with a revolver. The hosts explain the delay before the first award in 1901.

segments.title: Prize funding, cash value and Nobel Prize rules
segments.summary: The hosts explain that the prize is funded from investment interest, that it was about a million dollars at the start and is roughly that today, and that recipients customarily donate the money. They note there are no takebacks, no appeals, a limit of three laureates per year, and no posthumous awards.

segments.title: Norwegian Nobel Committee and selection process
segments.summary: The hosts describe the five-member Norwegian Nobel Committee, appointed by the Storting and now mostly retired politicians, and the nomination timeline from January through the October announcement and December ceremony in Oslo. They explain the research and vetting of nominees by advisors.

segments.title: Who can nominate, the medal, and the Branded tangent
segments.summary: The hosts explain that only certain national officials and credentialed people can nominate, and that you cannot nominate yourself. They describe the gold medal design by Gustav Vigeland, with Nobel's image and the Latin inscription, then digress briefly on the TV Western Branded.

segments.title: Eras, controversies and the Right Livelihood Award
segments.summary: The hosts discuss shifts in the committee's choices over time, the Kissinger and Le Duc Tho award where Le Duc Tho declined, Mandela and de Klerk, criticisms of Obama, Aung San Suu Kyi, Abiy Ahmed, and the Gandhi snub. They close with the Right Livelihood Award as an alternative and Nobel's stamp collection funding it.

segments.title: Wrap-up
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck agree the episode was good and move to listener mail.
